# Test Scenario: Stack Layout Direction

<!-- scenario-metadata:start: generated by `yarn sync-scenario-metadata` -->

| Field        | Value                         |
| ------------ | ----------------------------- |
| Key          | `test-stack-layout-direction` |
| Platforms    | Android, iOS                  |
| E2E coverage | TBD                           |
| Smoke test   | No                            |

| Device        | Test on            | Setup                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| iPhone        | iOS 18.6, iOS 27.2 | System RTL: an RTL system language (Arabic, Hebrew) with an RTL localization in the app (e.g. an empty `ar.lproj/InfoPlist.strings`), or launch the app with the arguments `-AppleTextDirection YES -NSForceRightToLeftWritingDirection YES` (Xcode: scheme → Run → Options → App Language → Right-to-Left Pseudolanguage). System LTR: English, launched without those arguments. |
| Android phone | API Level 37       | API 33 or newer for the push and pop steps (below API 33 the `default` animation is a zoom with no sideways motion).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

**E2E coverage details:** The probe and title bounds are readable with Detox, the back button side and the transition direction are not; not implemented yet.

<!-- scenario-metadata:end -->

## Description

Verify the `direction` prop of `StackHost`. Pass: with `ltr`
and `rtl` the header layout, the back button side and push and pop follow the
prop, also when it changes at runtime; with `inherit` the stack follows React
Native on Android and the system language on iOS. Header content insets under
RTL are covered by `test-stack-header-content-insets-android`.

## Note

- Wait for every transition to finish before the next tap.
- "forceRTL" and "allowRTL" take effect after a restart and are kept across
  launches. After a launch, "forceRTL" shows the `I18nManager.isRTL` value and
  "allowRTL" shows on, whatever is stored.
- **Known issue:** iOS: when "direction" differs from the system direction, the
  back button is on the right side, but its chevron and the order of the
  chevron and the title follow the system direction (iOS 26+: only with system
  RTL and `ltr`)
  (https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-screens-labs/issues/2074).
- **Known issue:** Android: turning "titleCentered" on does not move `L·48`; it
  keeps the gap from the edge it had before
  (https://github.com/software-mansion/react-native-screens-labs/issues/1835).

## Steps

### Baseline

1. Launch the app with system LTR and navigate to the **Stack Layout
   Direction** screen.

   - [ ] The screen shows `I18nManager.isRTL == false`.
   - [ ] "direction" reads `ltr`.
   - [ ] `L·48` is on the left edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] Android: the title "Direction" and the subtitle "Subtitle" are
         left-aligned, next to `L·48`.
   - [ ] iOS: the title "Direction" is centered.
   - [ ] iOS 26+: "Subtitle" is below the title.
   - [ ] The content row reads "START" on the left.

---

### System LTR / RN LTR

1. Set "direction" to `inherit`.

   - [ ] The header matches Baseline step 1.

2. Set "direction" to `rtl`.

   - [ ] `L·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the left edge.
   - [ ] Android: the title and the subtitle are right-aligned, next to `L·48`.
   - [ ] Android: the content row reads "START" on the right.
   - [ ] iOS: the content row still reads "START" on the left.

3. Tap "Push screen (adds a back button)".

   - [ ] The incoming screen enters from the left.
   - [ ] The covered screen moves to the right.
   - [ ] Android: the incoming screen fades in and moves only a short distance.
   - [ ] The back button is on the right edge.
   - [ ] The back button chevron points right.
   - [ ] iOS: `L·48` is next to the back button.
   - [ ] Android: `L·48` is next to the title.
   - [ ] iOS 18: the back button reads `> Direction` (see Note).
   - [ ] The header does not change after the transition ends.

4. Tap the back button.

   - [ ] The popped screen leaves toward the left.

5. Tap "Push screen (adds a back button)", then set "direction" to `ltr`.

   - [ ] The back button moves to the left edge.
   - [ ] The back button chevron points left.
   - [ ] iOS: `L·48` is next to the back button.
   - [ ] Android: `L·48` is next to the title.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the right edge.

6. Tap the back button.

   - [ ] The popped screen leaves toward the right.

7. Set "direction" to `rtl`, then tap "Push nested stack".

   - [ ] The "Outer" header has its back button on the right edge.
   - [ ] The "Nested" header has its `L·48` on the left edge.
   - [ ] The screen shows "nested direction: ltr".

8. Set "nested direction" to `inherit`.

   - [ ] The "Nested" header has its `L·48` on the right edge.
   - [ ] The "Outer" header does not change.

9. Tap the back button in the "Outer" header, then set "direction" to
   `inherit`.

   - [ ] The header matches Baseline step 1.

---

### System RTL / RN RTL

1. Turn "forceRTL" on, then restart the app with system RTL (iOS, see
   Setup) and navigate to the **Stack Layout Direction** screen.

   - [ ] The screen shows `I18nManager.isRTL == true`.
   - [ ] "direction" reads `rtl`.
   - [ ] `L·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the left edge.
   - [ ] The content row reads "START" on the right.

2. Set "direction" to `inherit`.

   - [ ] The header does not change.

3. Set "direction" to `ltr`.

   - [ ] `L·48` is on the left edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] Android: the content row reads "START" on the left.
   - [ ] iOS: the content row still reads "START" on the right.

4. Set "direction" to `rtl`, then tap "Push screen (adds a back button)".

   - [ ] The incoming screen enters from the left.
   - [ ] The back button is on the right edge.
   - [ ] The back button chevron points right.

5. Tap the back button, then turn "forceRTL" off.

   - [ ] The popped screen leaves toward the left.

---

### iOS only: System RTL / RN LTR

1. Turn "forceRTL" and "allowRTL" off, then restart the app with system RTL
   (see Setup) and navigate to the **Stack Layout Direction** screen.

   - [ ] The screen shows `I18nManager.isRTL == false`.
   - [ ] "direction" reads `ltr`.
   - [ ] `L·48` is on the left edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the right edge.

2. Set "direction" to `inherit`.

   - [ ] `L·48` moves to the right edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` moves to the left edge.

3. Set "direction" to `ltr`.

   - [ ] `L·48` is on the left edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the right edge.

4. Tap "Push screen (adds a back button)", then swipe from the right edge to
   the middle of the screen.

   - [ ] The pushed screen stays.
   - [ ] The back button is on the left edge.
   - [ ] The back button chevron points right (see Note).
   - [ ] iOS 18: the back button reads `Direction >` (see Note).

5. Swipe from the left edge to the middle of the screen.

   - [ ] The pushed screen follows the finger.
   - [ ] The pushed screen pops when released.

6. Set "direction" to `inherit`, then turn "allowRTL" off, then on.

   - [ ] `L·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the left edge.

---

### iOS only: System LTR / RN RTL

1. Turn "forceRTL" on, then restart the app with system LTR and navigate to the
   **Stack Layout Direction** screen.

   - [ ] The screen shows `I18nManager.isRTL == true`.
   - [ ] "direction" reads `rtl`.
   - [ ] `L·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the left edge.
   - [ ] The content row reads "START" on the right.

2. Set "direction" to `inherit`.

   - [ ] `L·48` moves to the left edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` moves to the right edge.
   - [ ] The content row still reads "START" on the right.

3. Set "direction" to `rtl`.

   - [ ] `L·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the left edge.

4. Tap "Push screen (adds a back button)", then swipe from the left edge to
   the middle of the screen.

   - [ ] The pushed screen stays.
   - [ ] The back button is on the right edge.
   - [ ] The back button chevron points right.
   - [ ] iOS 18: the back button reads `> Direction` (see Note).

5. Swipe from the right edge to the middle of the screen.

   - [ ] The pushed screen follows the finger.
   - [ ] The pushed screen pops when released.

6. Turn "forceRTL" off, restart the app and navigate to the **Stack Layout
   Direction** screen.

   - [ ] The screen matches Baseline step 1.

---

### Android only: Small header

1. Tap "Reset", then set "direction" to `rtl`.

   - [ ] The title and the subtitle are right-aligned.
   - [ ] `L·48` is next to the title, on the right.
   - [ ] `T·48` is on the left edge.

2. Turn "titleCentered" and "subtitleCentered" on.

   - [ ] The title and the subtitle are centered.
   - [ ] `L·48` does not move (see Note).

3. Turn "titleCentered" and "subtitleCentered" off, then set "menu" to
   `action + overflow`.

   - [ ] The title and the subtitle are right-aligned again.
   - [ ] From the left edge the order is `⋮`, "Act", `T·48`.
   - [ ] `L·48` is next to the title, on the right.

4. Turn "centerSubview" on.

   - [ ] `C·48` is centered in the bar.

5. Set "direction" to `ltr`.

   - [ ] The title and the subtitle are left-aligned.
   - [ ] `L·48` is next to the title, on the left.
   - [ ] `C·48` is still centered.
   - [ ] From the right edge the order is `⋮`, "Act", `T·48`.
   - [ ] The content row reads "START" on the left.

---

### Android only: Collapsing header

1. Turn "centerSubview" off, set "type" to `large`, then set "direction" to
   `rtl`.

   - [ ] `L·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] `T·48`, "Act" and `⋮` are on the left.
   - [ ] No header item is clipped.
   - [ ] The expanded title is large and on the right.

2. Set "expandedTitleHorizontalGravity" to `end`.

   - [ ] The expanded title moves to the left.

3. Set "expandedTitleHorizontalGravity" to `start`, then scroll down one full
   screen.

   - [ ] Only the toolbar row is left.
   - [ ] `L·48` is on the right edge.
   - [ ] `T·48`, "Act" and `⋮` are on the left.
   - [ ] The collapsed title is next to `L·48`.
   - [ ] The collapsed title covers neither `T·48` nor "Act".

4. Set "collapsedTitleHorizontalGravity" to `center`.

   - [ ] The collapsed title is centered between `L·48` and `T·48`.
   - [ ] The collapsed title covers neither `L·48` nor `T·48`.

5. Set "collapsedTitleHorizontalGravity" to `end`.

   - [ ] The collapsed title is next to `T·48`.
   - [ ] The collapsed title covers neither `T·48` nor "Act".

6. Set "collapsedTitleHorizontalGravity" to `start`, set "direction" to `ltr`,
   then scroll down one full screen.

   - [ ] `L·48` is on the left edge.
   - [ ] `T·48`, "Act" and `⋮` are on the right.
   - [ ] The collapsed title is next to `L·48`.

7. Scroll back to the top.

   - [ ] The header is fully expanded.
   - [ ] The expanded title is large and on the left.
   - [ ] `L·48` is on the left edge and not clipped.
